fact: The globular cluster 47 Tucanae lies in the southern constellation Tucana, about 14,700 light-years away.
bio: Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille found it from the Cape of Good Hope in 1751 and listed it as a nebula. N-body fits give it about 850,000 solar masses (Baumgardt's globular cluster database). More than 40 radio pulsars are known in it. Hubble photometry splits its main sequence in two: about 30% of the stars have primeval abundances and the rest are enriched in nitrogen and slightly in helium, so it holds more than one stellar population (Milone and colleagues, 2012).
